newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends at year high on heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends at year high on heavy trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Friday at a 1997 high for the second straight session in heavy trade pulled up by strong economic data released in Beijing during the day, analysts said.
The index was 6.54 points or 3.75 percent higher at 181.10, after surging to an intra-session high of 186.69 in early morning trading.
Turnover was at a 1997 high of HK$440.6 million against Thursday's HK$268.1 million.
"The statistics released by Beijing today helped push the index higher," an analyst at a western investment bank said.
China is expected to record gross domestic product growth (GDP) of 9.5 percent in the first half of 1997 and 10 percent for the whole year, the State Statistical Bureau said on Friday.
Retail price inflation is expected to be less than five percent for the year, the bureau said.

Analysts said another factor helping the Shenzhen B index to extend Thursday's 8.57 percent rise was the announcement from the central bank that the anti-inflation interest rate subsidy for May would be set at zero percent.

"Thanks to the statistics, together with the zero percent May interest rate subsidy, investors can reasonably expect loosened credit control by the government," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The foreign currency B share index is expected to continue upwards early next week judging from trade volumes today, analysts said.
"The index is going to gain second wind and may break through the 200-point level," a trader at China Southern Securities said.
The index shot up on Friday morning but then fell back to 175.79 points as investors briefly took profits, traders said.
The A share index added 0.65 points or 0.14 percent to end at 461.96 on turnover of 8.46 billion yuan.
"The upward trend sagged for a while this morning but it has not lost momentum," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
A newspaper report saying major fund managers in Hong Kong have set up funds for B share investment also fuelled buying, analysts said.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen (China) Enterprise Co Ltd was the best performer on Friday, gaining HK$0.51 at 10 percent limit-up to HK$5.59 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
